svg.text: M3 x 16 hex button head, buried. Section on the screw axis (x = 34.5), 12 mm magazine
Same ISO 7380 button head in both panels - only the recess changes. This face is the magazine's lower front edge, the one the rail closes over; the rail profile's lowest
point is y = -22.72 (blue band). Green dashed line = the shallowest point of the surrounding face, measured across the head footprint with a d5.7 probe.
INSERTION: this edge sweeps this way (-y) as the magazine is clicked onto the rail

g.text: the rail lip reaches in to here
Head sticks out past the lip.
BEFORE - head on a d6.2 spot-face
1.51 mm spring seat left only 2.31 mm of wall for the recess
the rail lip reaches in to here
AFTER - head in a d6.0 counterbore
0.41 mm seat frees 1.10 mm; head drops fully in

svg.text: LEFT: head top at y -24.25 - 1.34 mm past the face on this plane and 1.53 mm past the rail lip. In the rail's path; this is the snag.
RIGHT: head top at y -22.25. That is 0.66 mm below the face on this plane, 0.05 mm below the shallowest point of the surrounding face anywhere under the head, and 0.47 mm behind the rail lip.
Buy: M3 x 16 hex-socket button head, ISO 7380 (2 mm key) - the ones you already have. M3 x 14 and x 12 also fit; x 18 bottoms out. Nip it up by hand: only 1.40 mm of thread.
